questions.stem: What is the main environmental problem with sending waste to landfill?

options.text: Landfill sites are too expensive to build
Non-biodegradable waste persists for hundreds of years, and decomposing waste produces methane and toxic leachate
Landfill sites attract too many tourists
Landfill waste can be blown away by the wind

questions.explanation: Landfill waste takes up land, non-biodegradable materials persist for centuries, decomposing organic waste produces methane (a greenhouse gas), and rainwater passing through waste can create toxic leachate that contaminates groundwater.

questions.stem: Why is recycling metals such as aluminium and steel particularly beneficial?

options.text: Recycled metals are stronger than new metals
It uses much less energy than extracting metals from their ores, reducing CO2 emissions and conserving finite ore supplies
Recycled metals are a different colour
It is the only way to obtain metals

questions.explanation: Recycling aluminium uses about 95% less energy than extracting it from bauxite ore. This greatly reduces carbon dioxide emissions and conserves finite metal ore reserves.

questions.stem: What is a disadvantage of incinerating (burning) waste?

options.text: It takes up too much land
It can release toxic gases and particulates into the atmosphere if not properly controlled
It produces too much water
It makes the waste heavier

questions.explanation: Incineration can release harmful gases (including carbon dioxide, sulfur dioxide, and toxic fumes from burning plastics) and particulates. Modern incinerators use filters and scrubbers to reduce these emissions.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the 'reduce, reuse, recycle' hierarchy?

options.text: The three methods are equally important and can be done in any order
Reducing waste is the most effective, followed by reusing items, then recycling materials
Recycling is the most important step
Only recycling is necessary to solve waste problems

questions.explanation: The waste hierarchy prioritises reducing consumption first (preventing waste), then reusing items for their original purpose, and finally recycling materials into new products. Reducing is most effective because it prevents waste being created.

questions.stem: Why is recycling glass beneficial compared to making new glass?

options.text: Recycled glass is a different colour to new glass
It requires lower temperatures to melt, saving energy and reducing carbon dioxide emissions
Recycled glass is stronger than new glass
Glass cannot be recycled

questions.explanation: Recycled glass (cullet) melts at a lower temperature than raw materials, so less energy is needed. This reduces fossil fuel consumption and CO2 emissions. Glass can also be recycled indefinitely without loss of quality.

questions.stem: What is a challenge associated with recycling plastics?

options.text: Plastics are too heavy to transport
Different types of plastic must be sorted and separated, and some plastics degrade in quality when recycled
Plastics dissolve in water during recycling
All plastics can be recycled together without sorting

questions.explanation: There are many different types of plastic, and they must be sorted before recycling because mixing them produces inferior materials. Some plastics also degrade in quality each time they are recycled (downcycling).

questions.stem: How does recycling help conserve natural resources?

options.text: It creates new natural resources
It reduces the need to extract finite raw materials from the Earth
It increases the amount of fossil fuels available
It has no effect on natural resources

questions.explanation: By recycling materials like metals, glass, and paper, we reduce the need to mine ores, quarry sand, or cut down trees. This helps conserve finite natural resources for future generations.
